chapter_title: Clever of You to Figure It Out

segments.title: Clever of You to Figure It Out
segments.content:
In his youth, Li Luo was a stubborn one.

To the other four people present, imagining Li Luo apologizing was as ludicrous as Shao Heqi finally mustering the courage to confess his feelings, Jin Yuting sticking to a diet for a whole month, Zhao Rongjun taking the initiative to talk to a girl, or Ying Chanxi frantically chasing after a boy.

But at this very moment, it was actually happening.

It was only when Ying Chanxi happily agreed and Li Luo responded with a smile that the other three gradually came back to their senses.

"Wait... what's the point of you apologizing now?" The assistant class monitor, Shao Heqi, couldn't help but interject. "There's not even a full day left. Tomorrow are the exams for Chinese, Math, and Politics & History. Can you even cram it all in?"

"Yeah," the plump, freckle-faced Jin Yuting chimed in. "Chanxi, Li Luo pushed you to the ground just now. Is a simple apology really enough?"

"No matter how smart he is, there's no way he can get into the Fuyi High School with just one day of review."

"Aren't we going to be separated from him after this anyway? Why are you still helping him like this?"

Hearing what her two classmates were saying, Ying Chanxi just shook her head.

Fallen leaves on the street drifted with the wind, gliding past her hair. She then looked at Li Luo and smiled faintly, "So you know how to apologize now?"

"That slap of yours was well-deserved." Li Luo gave her a thumbs-up, not minding the stinging slap from his childhood friend in the slightest. He even praised her, "It completely knocked some sense into me."

Hearing Li Luo say this with such a happy smile, even Ying Chanxi was a little stunned.

The young girl subconsciously looked down at her fair, slender hands, wondering if that slap was really so effective.

With that thought, her gaze lifted back to Li Luo, and her eyes fell on the other, untouched side of his face.

This glance made Li Luo subconsciously take half a step back, covering his cheek with his hand as he stared at her warily. "Hey... what are you thinking of doing?"

"Um..." Seeing her thoughts so easily read by her childhood friend, Ying Chanxi felt a bit guilty and averted her gaze, quickly changing the subject. "Let's go, let's go. We need to hurry back and review."

"Tingting, you should head back early too. Get some good rest and relax. You can't slack off for the exams tomorrow and the day after."

"Oh, and Shao Heqi, you too. Good luck."

...

June in Yuhang City was already very hot.

After parting ways with the other three at the intersection, Li Luo and Ying Chanxi walked home together.

Ying Chanxi raised her hand to wipe her forehead. It was unclear whether she was wiping away sweat or secretly wiping away the traces of her earlier tears.

Although she was only wearing a simple, short-sleeved school uniform, Ying Chanxi at this moment was filled with a youthful, tender beauty.

The tips of her hair shimmered under the sunlight, and a few messy strands strayed by her ear. One lock fell, tracing the beautiful curve of her delicate chin.

The two of them walked in silence. Li Luo didn't say a word, his mind still recalling the events between the high school entrance exams and his rebirth.

For some reason, even though it was a distant past from nearly twenty years ago, Li Luo's memory of those former days was now incredibly clear.

He remembered.

In 2014, his parents were still running that small breakfast shop, working from dawn till dusk just to support his education.

His own entrance exam scores had been terrible, three points short of the cutoff for even the worst regular high school in Yuhang City's Yinjiang District.

If his parents hadn't asked a relative for a favor and paid a 30,000 yuan "school selection fee," plus an extra 3,000 yuan in tuition each year compared to regular students, he would have had to go to a vocational high school.

Even so, he didn't do well in high school. His grades showed no improvement, though he did pick up smoking and drinking.

After muddling through three years of high school, his college entrance exam results were a complete mess.

His parents arranged for him to go to a junior college, where he casually learned to cook. He interned at a restaurant for half a month before he couldn't take it anymore and quit.

He became an unemployed loafer.

And every unemployed young person fantasizes about being a writer.

So he tried writing web novels. After dabbling for a year or two, with the guidance and help of a kind author, he actually managed to make a small name for himself, earning four to five thousand yuan a month in royalties.

But he only produced that one book. After a series of failures, he went into shooting short dramas, struggling in the short video scene.

He even followed a musician for a while, writing short video scripts and learning some guitar on the side, able to play a few simple tunes.

Unfortunately, the short video market quickly became a red ocean. Unemployed again, Li Luo delivered food for a while, then went back to his cooking skills, selling fried rice noodles on the street for a few months.

He looked for a job during the day and sold fried noodles at night, barely managing to support himself.

But it was around that time that his mother fell seriously ill and needed a large sum of money for treatment.

His dad sold the breakfast shop's storefront and mortgaged their home.

Li Luo had little money himself, so he could only grovel and borrow from people he once knew.

At the same time, he also took a job as a Taobao customer service representative, pretending to be a young female assistant to chat with customers about styles, sizes, complain about ex-boyfriends, and console them that being a little small was cute too, earning whatever he could.

It was then that Ying Chanxi privately transferred ten thousand yuan to him and gave his father another one hundred thousand, covering the subsequent medical fee shortfall.

And then...

And then, everything had started over!

Li Luo turned his head to look at the childhood friend beside him, took a deep breath, feeling the air swell in his chest, and then slowly exhaled.

"Feeling nervous now?" Seeing him take such a deep breath, Ying Chanxi finally found an opening to break the silence. She couldn't help but say, "I offered to tutor you before, but you kept avoiding me."

Hearing Ying Chanxi's soft and slightly sticky tone, and the complaint and helplessness in her voice, Li Luo felt a little embarrassed.

"I know I was wrong. Aren't I trying to make up for it now?"

"This is the last day!" Seeing that his attitude wasn't as bad as before, Ying Chanxi couldn't help but raise her voice slightly. But in the next second, she quickly reined in her emotions, took a deep breath, and said slowly, "Anyway, let's walk faster."

"When we get back, take out your Chinese and Math papers from the first, second, and third mock exams."

"I'll go over your mistakes with you first."

There were a total of five subjects for the June high school entrance exam in Yuhang City.

Besides the usual Chinese, Math, and English, each worth 120 points, Physics and Chemistry were combined into a "Science" category, as a single subject with a total of 180 points.

The remaining subject was History and Politics, also a single subject, worth only 50 points.

Adding in the 30 points from the PE exam which was already completed, the total score for the high school entrance exam in Yuhang City's Yinjiang District was 620 points.

Last year, the admission score for the best high school in Yinjiang District, Yuhang Fuyi High School, was 507 points.

The lowest admission score for a regular high school was 421 points.

In other words, if Li Luo wanted to get into a regular high school, he only had about 200 points to spare out of the total 620.

Ying Chanxi remembered clearly that Li Luo's scores in the first three mock exams were 417, 401, and 425 respectively.

The third mock exam paper had been relatively easy, which was how he had barely managed to pass the regular high school cutoff line.

So even with only one day left, Ying Chanxi hoped Li Luo would review properly.

If he could just remember a few more formulas and vocabulary words, he might be able to scrape together a few more points and get over the regular high school cutoff.

As for Li Luo right now, the matter also made him a little nervous.

As the excitement of his rebirth gradually calmed down, Li Luo began to re-evaluate his current exam-taking abilities.

It felt a little worrying...

But at least he had been to high school in his past life. No matter how poorly he had studied, he should still have some of the high school knowledge framework. Applying that knowledge downwards, surely he wouldn't fail to even get into a regular high school, right?

Li Luo muttered to himself, feeling it might be a close call.

He then followed Ying Chanxi all the way into Jincheng Community.

Ying Chanxi took out her keys, opened the building's entrance door, and climbed the stairs to the fourth floor.

She then expertly lifted a flowerpot in the corner outside unit 401, retrieved a spare key from under the small mat beneath the pot, and opened the door to Li Luo's home.

Right.

Unit 402 across the hall was Ying Chanxi's home.

Unit 401 was Li Luo's.

But Ying Chanxi obviously knew Li Luo's place like the back of her hand. She walked in familiarly, changed into the small pink slippers Li Luo's mother had bought especially for her, and pattered into Li Luo's bedroom.

"Hurry up." Ying Chanxi's head poked out from his bedroom doorway, her long hair cascading down and swaying left and right like smooth silk. "Let's hurry, don't just stand there dazed."

Seeing this long-lost scene, Li Luo felt a wave of nostalgia.

Called back to his senses by Ying Chanxi, he quickly walked into his home, changed his slippers, and followed her into his bedroom.

Li Luo's bedroom was simple: a bed, a wardrobe, a desk, and two stools. That was it.

Later, during his two years in junior college, his family spent money to renovate the place, and Li Luo's bedroom became much brighter and cleaner.

Returning to this somewhat old and dim little bedroom now, Li Luo felt a bit emotional.

But Ying Chanxi didn't give him much time to be sentimental. She urged him to take out the papers from the three mock exams from his schoolbag, pull out the Chinese and Math sections, and slap them on the desk.

However, after sitting down, Ying Chanxi looked at the still very visible handprint on Li Luo's left cheek and suddenly felt a bit embarrassed. "Does your face still hurt? Do you want an ice pack?"

"It's alright." Li Luo touched his left cheek. The burning pain from before had subsided a lot. "You hit me so hard earlier, and now you're feeling shy?"

"Even though you apologized, you were still very annoying when you pushed me to the ground," Ying Chanxi huffed softly, then added an explanation, "I'm afraid Uncle and Auntie will see it. It would be hard to explain."

"Just tell them the truth."

"No way." Ying Chanxi shook her head repeatedly. "I never hit people."

"How can you say that with a straight face? How did you used to pull my ear?"

"If Uncle and Auntie don't know, then it didn't happen."

"Alright, alright, you're the model student, Ying Chanxi."

"Hmph." Ying Chanxi only showed this side of herself when bickering with Li Luo. But she quickly returned to her normal state, her small hand patting the table lightly. "Okay, let's start with the questions."

...

There are many differences between a poor student and a top student.

But in Ying Chanxi's opinion, the most important difference was that a poor student's knowledge of a subject was all fragmented, without a complete knowledge framework.

Take math, for instance.

It included sections like real numbers, algebra, geometry, equations, functions, and so on, all of which were interconnected.

In a semester with dozens of math classes, a poor student might have only listened to a few geometry problems, knowing how to solve for congruent triangles. But when they saw a function problem, their mind would go blank, feeling like they were looking at some alien language.

They had no complete framework of mathematical knowledge.

It was now the last day before the entrance exams.

Trying to help Li Luo build a junior high math knowledge framework in such a short time was nothing short of a fool's dream.

So Ying Chanxi's strategy was simple.

She directly skipped the last question of the multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and free-response sections.

When it came time for the actual exam, there was a ninety-nine percent chance Li Luo wouldn't be able to solve these most difficult problems anyway.

As for the especially simple problems, even if Li Luo got some of them right, Ying Chanxi would break them down and spoon-feed them to him.

To put it bluntly, they would give up all the points for difficult questions and get as many points as possible from the basic ones.

The approach for other subjects was similar.

"Tomorrow's exams are only Chinese, Math, and Politics & History, and Politics & History is an open-book exam, so today I'll focus on helping you review Chinese and Math."

Ying Chanxi said this, her expression particularly serious as she taught.

But the more they reviewed, the stranger Li Luo's expression became.

It wasn't that after nearly twenty years, he had returned all this knowledge to his teachers.

Rather... he seemed to remember everything he had learned back then with perfect clarity?!

"The line before 'My life's fortunes rise and fall like duckweed in the rain'?"

"'The mountains and rivers are broken, the wind scatters the catkins.'"

"'My chest heaves with rising clouds'?"

"'My eyes strain to follow the birds returning home.'"

"The two lines before 'Such things have been imperfect since ancient times'?"

"'People have sorrow and joy, separation and reunion; the moon has its dark and bright, its waxing and waning.'"

"Suddenly, he came upon a grove of peach blossoms. For several hundred paces along both banks..."

"...there were no other trees, only fragrant, beautiful grasses and a riot of falling petals. The fisherman was greatly surprised. He went on, wanting to see the end of the grove..."

"...He left his boat and entered through the opening. At first, it was extremely narrow, barely allowing a person to pass..."

"...He was never able to find it again. He fell ill and died. Afterward, no one else went searching for it."

Li Luo was immersed in his own memories, which were as clear as if he had a solid-state drive installed in his brain. He subconsciously recited the entirety of "The Peach Blossom Spring."

But when he came back to his senses, he realized something—

Even back in junior high, he had never completely memorized "The Peach Blossom Spring"!

At most, he had read it completely a few times and memorized some sentences that often appeared on exams.

What he had just done wasn't so much "reciting" as it was directly "reading" "The Peach Blossom Spring"!

"When did you secretly memorize this?" Ying Chanxi looked at him, astonished. "You dragged Zhao Rongjun to play basketball every day. Don't tell me you had him secretly help you review?"

"..." Faced with such a question, Li Luo found it a bit difficult to explain and fell silent for a moment.

"...Clever of you to figure it out."
